concept.description: For a quaternion algebra B over a number field F, there is an injection π′↦π from automorphic representations of B^×(A_F) that are not one-dimensional into cuspidal automorphic representations of GL₂(A_F), with π_v≅π′_v where B splits and π_v the essentially square-integrable representation corresponding to π′_v where B ramifies; its image consists of the π that are essentially square-integrable at every place where B ramifies. The local correspondence matches characters on regular elliptic elements.

concept.title: Integral models and bad reduction of Shimura curves
concept.description: For a Shimura curve M_K over a totally real field F attached to a quaternion algebra split at a finite place 𝔭 and level K=K^𝔭·K_𝔭 with K_𝔭 a principal congruence subgroup, Carayol constructs a regular model over O_(F,𝔭) via Drinfeld level structures on divisible O_𝔭-modules of height two; its special fibre is a union of Igusa-type curves meeting at supersingular points, whose completed local rings are universal deformation rings of formal O_𝔭-modules of height two with level structure.

concept.title: Vanishing cycles exact sequence for a curve over a henselian discrete valuation ring
concept.description: For a proper flat curve X over a henselian discrete valuation ring with special fibre X_s, generic geometric fibre X_η̄ and ℓ invertible, there is a Galois-equivariant long exact sequence relating H^i(X_s̄,Λ), H^i(X_η̄,Λ) and the vanishing cycles R^iΦΛ at the singular points; for semistable X the vanishing cycles are concentrated at the double points and the monodromy N is given by the Picard–Lefschetz formula (SGA 7).

concept.title: Semistable reduction theorem for curves
concept.description: A smooth proper geometrically connected curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring acquires semistable reduction after a finite separable extension of the base: it extends to a proper flat model whose special fibre is reduced with only ordinary double points (Deligne–Mumford).

concept.title: Universal deformations of formal modules with Drinfeld level structure
concept.description: For a nonarchimedean local field F with valuation ring O, a one-dimensional formal O-module of height h over the algebraic closure of the residue field has a universal deformation over a formal power series ring in h−1 variables over the completed maximal unramified extension of O (Lubin–Tate); adding Drinfeld level-𝔭^n structures gives finite flat regular local covers, carrying commuting actions of GL_h(O) and of the units of the division algebra of invariant 1/h (Drinfeld).

concept.title: Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms at almost all places
concept.description: For a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(A_F), F totally real, with archimedean components D_(k_τ,w), k_τ≥2 (and, for [F:ℚ] even, essentially square-integrable at some finite place), there is a strictly compatible system of two-dimensional λ-adic Galois representations whose restriction to the Weil group at almost every finite place corresponds to π_𝔭 by the Hecke correspondence; it is cut out from the ℓ-adic cohomology of Shimura curves via the Eichler–Shimura congruence relation (Ohta; Rogawski–Tunnell; for F=ℚ Eichler–Shimura–Deligne).

concept.title: Automorphic induction from a Hecke character of a quadratic extension
concept.description: For a quadratic extension L/F of number fields and a Hecke character ξ of A_L^× not factoring through the norm, the Weil representation construction gives a cuspidal automorphic representation π(ξ) of GL₂(A_F) whose local components are the representations attached to (L_v/F_v,ξ_v), so that its L-function is L(s,ξ) and at each place it corresponds to the induced representation of the local character (Jacquet–Langlands §12).

concept.title: Langlands base change for GL₂
concept.description: For a cyclic extension L/F of number fields of prime degree, every cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(A_F) has a base change Π to GL₂(A_L), automorphic, whose local components are the local base changes of π_v; at unramified places it corresponds to restriction of the Satake parameters, and locally base change corresponds to restriction of Weil–Deligne representations (Langlands 1980).

concept.title: Langlands–Tunnell theorem
concept.description: Every continuous two-dimensional complex representation of the absolute Galois group of a number field with solvable image, in particular of tetrahedral or octahedral projective type, is automorphic: there is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂ whose local components correspond to its local restrictions at every place (Artin conjecture for these representations).

concept.title: Globalization of primitive local Galois representations
concept.description: Given an irreducible primitive two-dimensional representation σ of the Weil group of a p-adic field F with finite image, there are a number field k, a place v₀ of k with k_(v₀)≅F, and a Galois representation of k of tetrahedral or octahedral projective type with finite image whose restriction to the decomposition group at v₀ is σ (Tunnell 1978, Theorem 1.3).

concept.title: Finite subgroups of PGL₂(ℂ)
concept.description: Every finite subgroup of PGL₂(ℂ)≅SO(3,ℂ) is cyclic, dihedral, or isomorphic to the tetrahedral group A₄, the octahedral group S₄ or the icosahedral group A₅.

concept.title: Local Galois representations of classical modular forms at bad primes via modular curves
concept.description: For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_ℚ) attached to a newform of weight ≥2 and every prime p≠ℓ at which the local component is not supercuspidal extraordinary, the restriction to the Weil group at p of its ℓ-adic Galois representation corresponds to the local component under the Hecke correspondence; this was proved by Langlands and Deligne from the bad reduction of modular curves (Deligne, 'Formes modulaires et représentations de GL(2)', and letter to Piatetski-Shapiro).

concept.title: Atom of a Markov chain
concept.description: For a Markov kernel P on a measurable space, a measurable set α is an atom if all its points have the same transition law: there is a probability measure ν with P(x,·)=ν for every x∈α. For a ψ-irreducible chain, an atom with ψ(α)>0 is called accessible.

concept.title: Maximal irreducibility measure of a Markov kernel
concept.description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel P, an irreducibility measure ψ′ is maximal if every irreducibility measure of P is absolutely continuous with respect to ψ′. Maximal irreducibility measures exist and are mutually absolutely continuous, so the sets of positive maximal measure depend only on P.

concept.title: Positive recurrent ψ-irreducible Markov chain
concept.description: A ψ-irreducible Markov chain is recurrent if ∑_{n≥1}Pⁿ(x,A)=∞ for every state x and every measurable set A of positive maximal irreducibility measure. It is positive recurrent if it is recurrent and admits an invariant probability measure.

concept.title: f-geometrically regular set of a Markov chain
concept.description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain and a measurable f≥1, a measurable set A is f-geometrically regular if for every measurable B of positive maximal irreducibility measure there is r>1 with sup_{x∈A}E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_B−1}f(X_k)r^k]<∞, where τ_B=inf{n≥1:X_n∈B} is the first return time to B. For f=1 such a set is called geometrically regular.

concept.title: m-skeleton of a Markov chain
concept.description: For an integer m≥1, the m-skeleton of a Markov chain with kernel P is the Markov chain with kernel Pᵐ, the m-fold iterate of P; observing a chain (X_n) at the times 0,m,2m,… gives the m-skeleton (X_{mn}).

concept.title: Petite sets have maximal irreducibility minorizations
concept.description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel P on a countably generated state space, every petite set A is ψ_b-petite for some sampling distribution b: ∑_n b(n)Pⁿ(x,·)≥ψ_b on A, where ψ_b is a maximal irreducibility measure. Consequently inf_{x∈A}P_x(τ_B<∞)>0 for every set B of positive maximal irreducibility measure.

concept.title: Cyclic decomposition of a ψ-irreducible Markov chain
concept.description: Let P be ψ-irreducible with ψ maximal, and let C be a ν_M-small set with ψ(C)>0 and ν_M(C)>0. Let d be the greatest common divisor of E_C={n≥1: Pⁿ(x,·)≥δ_nν_M on C for some δ_n>0}. Then there are disjoint measurable D_1,…,D_d with P(x,D_{i+1})=1 for x∈D_i (indices mod d) and ψ-null complement of their union; d is the largest length of such a cycle, independent of C. Hence the chain is aperiodic exactly when d=1.

concept.title: Nonempty absorbing sets of a ψ-irreducible chain are full
concept.description: If a Markov chain is ψ-irreducible, every nonempty absorbing set A is full: its complement is null for a maximal irreducibility measure.

concept.title: Sublevel sets of a drift function towards a petite set are petite
concept.description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain, if V:X→[0,∞] satisfies PV≤V−1+b1_C for a petite set C and b<∞, then every sublevel set {V≤ℓ} with ℓ<∞ is petite: V is unbounded off petite sets. In particular this holds when V≥1 satisfies the geometric drift PV≤(1−β)V+b1_C with β>0.

concept.title: Regular sets of a ψ-irreducible chain are petite
concept.description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain on a countably generated state space, call a measurable set A regular if sup_{x∈A}E_x[τ_B]<∞ for every measurable B of positive maximal irreducibility measure, with τ_B the first return time to B. Every regular set is petite.

concept.title: Sure return to a set implies infinitely many returns
concept.description: For a Markov chain and a measurable set A with first return time τ_A=inf{n≥1:X_n∈A}, if P_x(τ_A<∞)=1 for every x∈A, then for every initial state x the probability of visiting A infinitely often equals P_x(τ_A<∞); in particular A is visited infinitely often almost surely from each of its points.

concept.title: Skeletons of an aperiodic ψ-irreducible Markov chain
concept.description: If a Markov chain on a countably generated state space is ψ-irreducible and aperiodic, then every m-skeleton (the chain with kernel Pᵐ) is ψ-irreducible and aperiodic, and some m-skeleton is strongly aperiodic: there are a set A and a measure ν with ν(A)>0 and Pᵐ(x,·)≥ν for every x∈A.

concept.title: Regenerative decomposition for a Markov chain with an atom
concept.description: Let a positive Harris recurrent Markov chain with invariant probability π have an accessible atom α with first return time τ_α. Put a_λ(n)=P_λ(τ_α=n), u(n)=Pⁿ(α,α) and t_f(n)=E_α[f(X_n)1{τ_α≥n}]. Then for every initial law λ, f≥0 and n≥1, |E_λf(X_n)−π(f)|≤E_λ[f(X_n)1{τ_α≥n}]+(|a_λ∗u−π(α)|∗t_f)(n)+π(α)∑_{j>n}t_f(j), where ∗ is convolution of sequences on the positive integers.

concept.title: Geometric convergence at a Kendall atom
concept.description: If a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov chain has an accessible atom α that is a Kendall atom, E_α[κ^{τ_α}]<∞ for some κ>1 with τ_α the first return time, then the chain has an invariant probability π and there are r>1 and R<∞ with |Pⁿ(α,α)−π(α)|≤Rr^{−n} for every n≥0.

concept.title: Erdős–Feller–Pollard renewal theorem
concept.description: Let p be a probability distribution on the positive integers whose support has greatest common divisor 1 and whose mean is m≤∞, and define the renewal sequence u(0)=1, u(n)=∑_{k=1}^{n}p(k)u(n−k). Then u(n)→1/m as n→∞, with 1/m=0 when m=∞.

concept.title: Return-time representation of the invariant measure of a recurrent chain
concept.description: For a recurrent ψ-irreducible Markov chain on a countably generated state space, the invariant measure π is unique up to constant multiples and equivalent to a maximal irreducibility measure, and for every set A of positive maximal irreducibility measure and measurable B, π(B)=∫_Aπ(dy)E_y[∑_{k=1}^{τ_A}1_B(X_k)]=∫_Aπ(dy)E_y[∑_{k=0}^{τ_A−1}1_B(X_k)], where τ_A is the first return time to A.

concept.title: Petite sets admit sampling distributions with finite mean
concept.description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel on a countably generated state space, every petite set is also petite for a uniform sampling distribution on {1,…,m} for some m, or for a geometric sampling distribution a_ε(n)=(1−ε)εⁿ; either choice has finite mean ∑_n n a(n).

concept.title: Spanning of the symmetric subspace by tensor powers
concept.description: For n,t≥1, the symmetric subspace Sym^t(ℂⁿ)⊆(ℂⁿ)^(⊗t) is the linear span of the tensor powers v^(⊗t), v∈ℂⁿ. Indeed it suffices to take v with all coordinates in any fixed set A⊆ℂ with at least t+1 elements.

concept.title: Averaging projection onto the invariant vectors of a unitary representation
concept.description: Let G be a group with a left-invariant probability measure μ, such as normalized Haar measure on a compact group or the uniform measure on a finite group, and let R be a unitary representation of G on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space V with g↦R(g) measurable. Then Π=∫_G R(g)dμ(g) is the orthogonal projection onto the fixed subspace V^G={v:R(g)v=v for all g∈G}.

concept.title: Number of multisets of a given size (stars and bars)
concept.description: For integers n≥1 and k≥0, the number of multisets of size k with elements from an n-element set, equivalently of functions φ:{1,…,n}→ℕ with φ(1)+⋯+φ(n)=k, is binom(n+k−1,k)=binom(n+k−1,n−1).

concept.title: Oseledets multiplicative ergodic theorem for real matrix cocycles
concept.description: Let T preserve a probability measure on X and let A:X→GL(d,ℝ) be measurable with log‖A‖ and log‖A⁻¹‖ integrable; put A_n(x)=A(Tⁿ⁻¹x)⋯A(x). For almost every x the limit Λ(x)=lim_n(A_n(x)ᵀA_n(x))^(1/2n) exists. If e^(χ₁)<⋯<e^(χ_s) are its eigenvalues, with eigenspaces of dimensions k_i, and V_i is the sum of the eigenspaces for χ₁,…,χ_i, then lim n⁻¹log‖A_n(x)v‖=χ_i for v∈V_i∖V_(i−1). The exponents and multiplicities are T-invariant functions, and ∑k_iχ_i=lim n⁻¹log|det A_n(x)|.

concept.title: Ergodicity of Bernoulli shifts on a finite alphabet
concept.description: For a finite set S and a probability vector p with positive entries, the left shift T on S^ℕ preserves the Bernoulli measure μ, determined by μ[a₀,…,a_(n−1)]=p_(a₀)⋯p_(a_(n−1)) on cylinders, and is mixing: μ(E∩T⁻ᵏF)→μ(E)μ(F) for all measurable E,F. In particular (S^ℕ,μ,T) is ergodic.

concept.title: Locally finite k-linear abelian category
concept.description: A k-linear abelian category over a field k is locally finite if every morphism space is finite-dimensional and every object has finite length.

concept.title: Finite k-linear abelian category
concept.description: A k-linear abelian category is finite if it is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional left modules over a finite-dimensional associative k-algebra.

concept.title: Multitensor category
concept.description: A locally finite k-linear abelian rigid monoidal category whose tensor product bifunctor is bilinear on morphisms. The unit object need not be simple; a finite multitensor category is one whose underlying abelian category is finite.

concept.title: Dual category of a module category over a multitensor category
concept.description: For a module category M over a multitensor category C, the dual category C*_M=Fun_C(M,M) is the category of right exact C-module endofunctors of M and module natural transformations, made monoidal by composition of functors.

concept.title: Deligne tensor product of multitensor categories
concept.description: For multitensor categories C and D over k, the Deligne tensor product C⊠D is a multitensor category with tensor product determined by (X⊠Y)⊗(X′⊠Y′)=(X⊗X′)⊠(Y⊗Y′), unit 1⊠1, and associativity constraints and duals induced from those of C and D.

concept.title: Existence and exactness of the Deligne tensor product
concept.description: For locally finite k-linear abelian categories C and D, a Deligne tensor product C⊠D exists, is locally finite and is unique up to unique equivalence; for coalgebras it is (C⊗D)-comod. The functor ⊠ is exact in each variable with Hom(X₁⊠X₂,Y₁⊠Y₂)≅Hom(X₁,Y₁)⊗Hom(X₂,Y₂), and bilinear bifunctors exact in each variable induce exact functors on C⊠D.

concept.title: Module endofunctors of the regular module category
concept.description: For a multitensor category C regarded as a left module category over itself, every C-module endofunctor of C is isomorphic to right tensoring −⊗X by an object X, with module structure given by the associativity constraint, and X↦(−⊗X) is a tensor equivalence C^op→C*_C.

concept.title: Stochastic Fubini theorem for continuous semimartingales
concept.description: Let X be a continuous semimartingale, μ a finite measure on a measurable space A, and H(a,t,ω) bounded and measurable for the product of the σ-algebra of A with the predictable σ-algebra. Then a↦∫₀ᵗH(a,s)dX_s has a measurable version and ∫_A(∫₀ᵗH(a,s)dX_s)μ(da)=∫₀ᵗ(∫_AH(a,s)μ(da))dX_s almost surely.

concept.title: Representation of a convex function by its second-derivative measure
concept.description: If f:ℝ→ℝ is convex and the Stieltjes measure f″(da) of its left derivative is finite, then there are constants α,β with f(x)=α+βx+½∫|x−a|f″(da) and f′₋(x)=β+½∫sgn(x−a)f″(da) for all x, where sgn(0)=−1.

concept.title: Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian manifold
concept.description: For a Riemannian manifold (M,g) with Levi-Civita connection ∇ and R(X,Y)=∇_X∇_Y−∇_Y∇_X−∇_[X,Y], the (0,4)-tensor Rm(X,Y,Z,W)=g(R(X,Y)W,Z), normalized so that Rm(e₁,e₂,e₁,e₂) is the sectional curvature of an orthonormal pair (the convention of Brendle–Schoen, who write R(X,Y,Z,W) and R_ijkl). At each point it is an algebraic curvature tensor: antisymmetric in each pair, symmetric under exchanging the pairs, and satisfying the first Bianchi identity.

concept.title: Algebraic curvature tensor on a Euclidean vector space
concept.description: A 4-linear form R on a Euclidean space V≅ℝⁿ with R(x,y,z,w)=−R(y,x,z,w)=−R(x,y,w,z)=R(z,w,x,y) and R(x,y,z,w)+R(y,z,x,w)+R(z,x,y,w)=0. Equivalently a self-adjoint endomorphism of ∧²V satisfying the first Bianchi identity (an algebraic curvature operator); the space of these is written S²_B(so(n)) and carries the natural action of O(n). The curvature tensor of a Riemannian manifold at a point is an algebraic curvature tensor.

concept.title: First Bianchi identity for the Riemann curvature tensor
concept.description: The Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian manifold (more generally of any torsion-free connection) satisfies R(X,Y)Z+R(Y,Z)X+R(Z,X)Y=0; in covariant form Rm(x,y,z,w)+Rm(y,z,x,w)+Rm(z,x,y,w)=0.

concept.title: Sectional curvature of a two-plane
concept.description: For a two-plane π⊂T_pM spanned by an orthonormal pair e₁,e₂, the sectional curvature is K(π)=Rm(e₁,e₂,e₁,e₂), independent of the orthonormal basis of π; the same formula defines the sectional curvatures of an algebraic curvature tensor. Positive (nonnegative) sectional curvature means K(π)>0 (≥0) for all two-planes.

concept.title: Ricci curvature tensor
concept.description: The symmetric 2-tensor Ric(x,y)=Σᵢ Rm(x,eᵢ,y,eᵢ), the trace of the curvature tensor over an orthonormal basis eᵢ; it is defined for Riemannian manifolds and for algebraic curvature tensors. Its trace-free part is Ric₀=Ric−(scal/n)g. Positive Ricci curvature means Ric(x,x)>0 for x≠0.

concept.title: Scalar curvature
concept.description: The trace scal=Σᵢ Ric(eᵢ,eᵢ) of the Ricci tensor with respect to the metric; for an algebraic curvature tensor it is Σ_{i,j}R(eᵢ,eⱼ,eᵢ,eⱼ).

concept.title: Curvature operator of an algebraic curvature tensor
concept.description: The self-adjoint endomorphism ℛ of ∧²T_pM (or of ∧²ℝⁿ for an algebraic curvature tensor R) determined by ⟨ℛ(x∧y),z∧w⟩=R(x,y,z,w), so that R(φ,φ)=⟨ℛφ,φ⟩ is a quadratic form on two-vectors. The curvature operator is nonnegative (positive) if R(φ,φ)≥0 (>0) for all φ≠0; nonnegative curvature operator implies nonnegative sectional curvature.

concept.title: Spherical space form
concept.description: A Riemannian manifold Sⁿ/Γ obtained as the quotient of the round unit sphere by a finite subgroup Γ⊂O(n+1) acting freely, with the induced metric of constant sectional curvature 1; up to scaling these are exactly the compact connected Riemannian manifolds of constant positive sectional curvature.

concept.title: Killing–Hopf theorem for constant positive curvature
concept.description: A complete connected Riemannian n-manifold (n≥2) of constant sectional curvature 1 is isometric to Sⁿ/Γ for a finite subgroup Γ⊂O(n+1) acting freely on Sⁿ; in particular a simply connected one is isometric to the round unit sphere.

concept.title: Isometry group of a Riemannian manifold
concept.description: The group Isom(M,g) of diffeomorphisms F:M→M with F*g=g, under composition.

concept.title: Pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvature
concept.description: A Riemannian manifold has pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures if its sectional curvatures are positive and at every point p, 0<K(π₁)<4K(π₂) for all two-planes π₁,π₂⊂T_pM; the ratio bound is required at each point separately, so no global curvature bounds are assumed.

concept.title: Positive and nonnegative isotropic curvature
concept.description: An algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ, n≥4, has nonnegative isotropic curvature if R₁₃₁₃+R₁₄₁₄+R₂₃₂₃+R₂₄₂₄−2R₁₂₃₄≥0 for every orthonormal four-frame {e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄}, and positive isotropic curvature (PIC) if the inequality is always strict; a Riemannian manifold of dimension at least four has PIC if its curvature tensor does at every point. Equivalently, the complexified curvature is positive on totally isotropic two-planes span{e₁+ie₂,e₃+ie₄} of T_pM⊗ℂ.

concept.title: Ricci flow
concept.description: A smooth one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics g(t) on a manifold M satisfying ∂g/∂t=−2Ric_{g(t)}, introduced by Hamilton in 1982.

concept.title: Normalized Ricci flow
concept.description: On a compact n-manifold, the volume-preserving flow ∂g/∂t=−2Ric_{g(t)}+(2/n)r_{g(t)}g(t), where r_{g(t)} is the mean value of the scalar curvature of g(t); its solutions differ from Ricci flows by rescaling the metric and reparametrizing time.

concept.title: Hamilton's evolution equation for the curvature tensor under Ricci flow
concept.description: Under Ricci flow, the curvature tensor written in an orthonormal frame evolving with the metric (Uhlenbeck's trick) satisfies ∂R/∂t=ΔR+Q(R), where Q(R)_{ijkl}=R_{ijpq}R_{klpq}+2R_{ipkq}R_{jplq}−2R_{iplq}R_{jpkq} is an O(n)-equivariant quadratic map on algebraic curvature tensors. The associated ODE dR/dt=Q(R) on S²_B(so(n)) is Hamilton's curvature ODE.

concept.title: Hamilton's maximum principle for curvature conditions under Ricci flow
concept.description: Let g(t) be a Ricci flow on a compact manifold and K a closed, convex, O(n)-invariant set of algebraic curvature tensors that is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R). If the curvature tensor of g(0) lies in K at every point (in orthonormal frames), then the curvature tensor of g(t) lies in K at every point for all t in the interval of existence. This is the Ricci-flow case of Hamilton's maximum principle for reaction–diffusion systems on vector bundles (Hamilton 1986, Theorem 4.3).

concept.title: Short-time existence and uniqueness of Ricci flow on compact manifolds
concept.description: For every smooth Riemannian metric g₀ on a compact manifold there is T>0 and a smooth Ricci flow g(t), t∈[0,T), with g(0)=g₀, and any two such flows agree on their common interval (Hamilton 1982; simplified proof via DeTurck's trick). By uniqueness and diffeomorphism invariance of the equation, isometries of g₀ remain isometries of every g(t).

concept.title: Kulkarni–Nomizu product of symmetric bilinear forms
concept.description: For symmetric bilinear forms A,B on ℝⁿ, the 4-tensor (A⊙B)_{ijkl}=A_{ik}B_{jl}−A_{il}B_{jk}−A_{jk}B_{il}+A_{jl}B_{ik}, which is an algebraic curvature tensor; with this normalization I=½ id⊙id is the curvature tensor of the round unit sphere.

concept.title: Böhm–Wilking linear transformation ℓ_{a,b} of algebraic curvature tensors
concept.description: For real a,b, the linear map ℓ_{a,b}(R)=R+b Ric₀⊙id+(a/n) scal id⊙id on algebraic curvature tensors on ℝⁿ, as printed by Brendle–Schoen; Böhm–Wilking display it as R+2(n−1)a R_I+(n−2)b R_{Ric₀}, and the parameter curves used in Brendle–Schoen Propositions 13-14 coincide with those of Böhm–Wilking Lemmas 3.4-3.5. Böhm and Wilking showed that ℓ_{a,b}^{-1}Q(ℓ_{a,b}R)−Q(R) does not depend on the Weyl part of R and is computable from the Ricci tensor, which allows Q-invariant cones to be deformed into new invariant cones.

concept.title: Böhm–Wilking invariant cones ℓ_{a,b}(nonnegative curvature operators with Ricci pinching)
concept.description: Böhm–Wilking (Ann. of Math. 2008, Lemmas 3.4–3.5): for b∈[0,1/2] with a=((n−2)b²+2b)/(2+2(n−2)b²), p=(n−2)b²/(1+(n−2)b²), and for b=1/2, a=(1+s)/2, p=1−4/(n+2+4s), s≥0, the sets ℓ_{a,b}({R≥0 : Ric≥(p/n) scal}) built from the cone of nonnegative curvature operators are invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R), transversally so for b>0; together they join the nonnegative cone to cones shrinking to the ray of the round-sphere curvature tensor.

concept.title: Pinching family of cones (Böhm–Wilking)
concept.description: Böhm–Wilking (2008, §3): a continuous family C(s), s∈[0,1), of closed convex O(n)-invariant full-dimensional cones of algebraic curvature tensors such that every nonzero element has positive scalar curvature, Q(R) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of C(s) at every nonzero R∈C(s) for s∈(0,1), and C(s) converges in the pointed Hausdorff topology to the ray ℝ₊I of the round-sphere curvature tensor as s→1.

concept.title: Böhm–Wilking convergence theorem for pinching families
concept.description: Böhm–Wilking (Ann. of Math. 2008, Theorem 5.1): let C(s), s∈[0,1), be a pinching family of cones in dimension n≥3. If the curvature tensor of a compact Riemannian manifold (M,g₀) lies in the interior of C(0) at every point, then the normalized Ricci flow from g₀ exists for all time and converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature.

concept.title: Hamilton's convergence theorem for Ricci flow with curvature in a pinching set
concept.description: Hamilton (J. Differential Geom. 1986, §5): if the curvature tensor of a compact Riemannian manifold (M,g₀) lies at every point in a pinching set, a closed convex O(n)-invariant set of algebraic curvature tensors preserved by dR/dt=Q(R) on which the trace-free part of R becomes small relative to the scalar curvature as the curvature grows, then the normalized Ricci flow from g₀ exists for all time and converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature. The exact quantitative form of Hamilton's pinching condition is not verified here.

concept.title: Tangent cone of a closed convex set
concept.description: For a closed convex set C in a finite-dimensional real vector space and x∈C, the tangent cone T_xC is the closure of ⋃_{t>0} t(C−x); a vector in the interior of T_xC points strictly into C.

concept.title: Berger's curvature inequality
concept.description: If all sectional curvatures of an algebraic curvature tensor R (for example of a Riemannian manifold at a point) lie in [K_min,K_max], then |R(e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄)|≤(2/3)(K_max−K_min) and |R(e₁,e₂,e₁,e₃)|≤(1/2)(K_max−K_min) for all orthonormal e₁,…,e₄.

concept.title: Orthogonal normal form of a real skew-symmetric bilinear form
concept.description: For a skew-symmetric bilinear form ω on a Euclidean space, equivalently a real skew-symmetric matrix or a two-vector, there is an orthonormal basis v₁,…,v_n with ω=a₁v₁∧v₂+a₂v₃∧v₄+⋯; that is, the matrix is block diagonal with 2×2 blocks [[0,a_k],[−a_k,0]] and zeros. On ℝ⁴ the basis may be taken positively oriented.

concept.title: Self-dual and anti-self-dual two-forms in dimension four
concept.description: On an oriented four-dimensional Euclidean space V the Hodge star *:∧²V→∧²V satisfies *²=1 and φ∧ψ=⟨*φ,ψ⟩vol; ∧²V splits orthogonally into the three-dimensional eigenspaces ∧²₊ (self-dual, *φ=φ) and ∧²₋ (anti-self-dual, *φ=−φ), and φ∧φ=(|φ₊|²−|φ₋|²)vol.

concept.title: Brendle–Schoen differentiable sphere theorem for pointwise 1/4-pinched manifolds
concept.description: A compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures (at each point 0<K(π₁)<4K(π₂) for all two-planes) admits a metric of constant positive sectional curvature, and is therefore diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. In particular a compact simply connected manifold whose sectional curvatures lie in (1,4] is diffeomorphic to Sⁿ, settling the differentiable version of the Rauch–Berger–Klingenberg sphere theorem. The proof deforms the metric by the normalized Ricci flow.

concept.title: Equivariant differentiable sphere theorem for pointwise 1/4-pinched manifolds
concept.description: Let M be a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures, G a compact Lie group and ρ:G→Isom(M) a homomorphism. Then there are a homomorphism σ:G→O(n+1) and a diffeomorphism F:M→Sⁿ with F∘ρ(g)=σ(g)∘F for all g∈G. It follows because the normalized Ricci flow deforms the metric canonically, hence G-equivariantly, to a round metric.

concept.title: Brendle–Schoen convergence theorem for Ricci flow under positive complex sectional curvature (strict PIC2)
concept.description: Let (M,g₀) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 such that R₁₃₁₃+λ²R₁₄₁₄+μ²R₂₃₂₃+λ²μ²R₂₄₂₄−2λμR₁₂₃₄>0 for all orthonormal four-frames and all λ,μ∈[−1,1]; equivalently, at every point the curvature tensor lies in the interior of the cone of tensors whose zero extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature, i.e. g₀ has positive complex sectional curvature. Then the normalized Ricci flow from g₀ exists for all time and converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature.

concept.title: Preservation of positive isotropic curvature under Ricci flow in all dimensions
concept.description: For n≥4, the set of algebraic curvature tensors on ℝⁿ with nonnegative isotropic curvature is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R); consequently, on a compact manifold of dimension n≥4, nonnegative isotropic curvature and positive isotropic curvature of g(0) are preserved along the Ricci flow g(t).

concept.title: Nonnegative complex sectional curvature (PIC2 cone Ĉ)
concept.description: An algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ has nonnegative complex sectional curvature if R(Z,W,Z̄,W̄)≥0 for all Z,W∈ℂⁿ, with R extended complex-multilinearly. Equivalently, its zero extension R̂ to ℝⁿ×ℝ², the curvature tensor of M×ℝ², has nonnegative isotropic curvature (Ni–Wolfson 2007, Prop. 5.1, after N. Wallach and a communication from Brendle–Schoen). These tensors form a closed convex O(n)-invariant cone Ĉ that contains every nonnegative curvature operator and lies in the cone of nonnegative sectional curvature; its interior is positive complex sectional curvature (strict PIC2).

concept.title: PIC1 condition: positive isotropic curvature of M×ℝ
concept.description: For an algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ let R̃ be its extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ by zero in the added direction, i.e. the curvature tensor of M×ℝ. R satisfies PIC1 if R̃ has positive isotropic curvature (nonnegative PIC1 if R̃ has nonnegative isotropic curvature). PIC1 implies R₁₂₁₂+R₁₃₁₃>0 for all orthonormal three-frames (2-positive flag curvature) and hence positive Ricci curvature.

concept.title: Ricci flow preserves nonnegative complex sectional curvature (PIC2)
concept.description: For n≥4, the cone Ĉ of algebraic curvature tensors whose zero extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature (equivalently, nonnegative complex sectional curvature) is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R), because zero extension commutes with Q; hence the condition is preserved by Ricci flow on compact manifolds. The same argument on ℝⁿ×ℝ shows that PIC1 is preserved.

concept.title: Brendle–Schoen characterization of the PIC2 condition
concept.description: For an algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ (n≥4), the zero extension R̂ to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature if and only if R(e₁,e₃,e₁,e₃)+λ²R(e₁,e₄,e₁,e₄)+μ²R(e₂,e₃,e₂,e₃)+λ²μ²R(e₂,e₄,e₂,e₄)−2λμR(e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄)≥0 for all orthonormal four-frames {e₁,…,e₄} of ℝⁿ and all λ,μ∈[−1,1].

concept.title: Pointwise 1/4-pinched curvature implies nonnegative complex sectional curvature
concept.description: If all sectional curvatures of an algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ lie in [κ,4κ] with κ≥0, then R has nonnegative complex sectional curvature; equivalently, its zero extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature. If the sectional curvatures are strictly pointwise 1/4-pinched, R has positive complex sectional curvature. Yau–Zheng (1991) state the sign-reversed form for negatively 1/4-pinched curvature.

concept.title: Böhm–Wilking pinching set theorem
concept.description: Böhm–Wilking (Ann. of Math. 2008, Theorem 4.1): given a continuous family C(s), s∈[0,1), of closed convex O(n)-invariant full-dimensional cones whose nonzero elements have positive scalar curvature and on whose nonzero elements Q points into the interior of the tangent cone for s∈(0,1), and given ε,h₀>0, there is a closed convex O(n)-invariant set F, invariant under dR/dt=Q(R), with C(ε)∩{tr R≤h₀}⊂F and F∖C(s) bounded for every s∈[ε,1) (a generalized pinching set).

concept.title: Rauch–Berger–Klingenberg topological sphere theorem
concept.description: A compact simply connected Riemannian n-manifold whose sectional curvatures lie in (1,4] is homeomorphic to Sⁿ. Rauch posed the problem and proved a version with a stronger pinching constant; Berger and Klingenberg proved the 1/4-pinched statement around 1960 by comparison geometry.

concept.title: Globally δ-pinched Riemannian manifold
concept.description: For 0<δ≤1, a Riemannian manifold is globally δ-pinched if, after scaling, all its sectional curvatures at all points lie in (1,1/δ]; for δ=1/4 this is the hypothesis of the topological sphere theorem.

concept.title: Gromoll–Calabi differentiable sphere theorem
concept.description: For each n there is δ(n)∈(0,1), with δ(n)→1 as n→∞, such that every compact simply connected globally δ(n)-pinched Riemannian n-manifold is diffeomorphic to Sⁿ (Gromoll 1966, and independently Calabi). Later work (Sugimoto–Shiohama–Karcher, Ruh, Grove–Karcher–Ruh) obtained pinching constants independent of n.

concept.title: Grove–Karcher–Ruh equivariant sphere theorem
concept.description: There is a universal constant δ<1 (δ=0.98 in the original, later improved by Im Hof–Ruh) such that if a compact Lie group G acts by isometries on a compact simply connected globally δ-pinched Riemannian n-manifold M, then M is G-equivariantly diffeomorphic to Sⁿ with a linear orthogonal G-action.

concept.title: Hamilton's theorem on three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature
concept.description: A compact three-manifold with a Riemannian metric of positive Ricci curvature admits a metric of constant positive sectional curvature: the normalized Ricci flow exists for all time and converges to such a metric (Hamilton 1982).

concept.title: Hamilton's theorem on four-manifolds with positive curvature operator
concept.description: A compact four-manifold with a metric of positive curvature operator is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form (S⁴ or ℝP⁴): the normalized Ricci flow converges to a constant curvature metric (Hamilton 1986).

concept.title: H. Chen's theorem on four-manifolds with 2-positive curvature operator
concept.description: H. Chen (Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 1991): a compact four-manifold with 2-positive curvature operator is diffeomorphic to S⁴ or ℝP⁴ (via Ricci flow), and a compact pointwise 1/4-pinched four-manifold is diffeomorphic to S⁴ or ℝP⁴ or, in the weakly pinched case, isometric to ℂP² up to scaling.

concept.title: Andrews–Nguyen theorem on four-manifolds with 1/4-pinched flag curvature
concept.description: Compact four-manifolds with pointwise 1/4-pinched flag curvature (in the sense of Andrews–Nguyen) are diffeomorphic to spherical space forms; proved with the Ricci flow.

concept.title: Huisken's theorem: sufficiently pinched manifolds are space forms
concept.description: For each n≥4 there is ε(n)>0 such that a compact n-manifold of positive scalar curvature whose curvature tensor is pointwise ε(n)-close to constant curvature, in the sense that the Weyl and trace-free Ricci parts are small relative to the scalar curvature, is deformed by the normalized Ricci flow to a metric of constant curvature (Huisken 1985; also Margerin, Nishikawa).

concept.title: Böhm–Wilking theorem: manifolds with 2-positive curvature operator are space forms
concept.description: On a compact Riemannian manifold with 2-positive curvature operator (in particular positive curvature operator), the normalized Ricci flow converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature, so the manifold is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form (Böhm–Wilking, Ann. of Math. 2008). The theorem was previously known in dimensions at most four (Hamilton, Chen).

concept.title: Micallef–Moore sphere theorem for positive isotropic curvature
concept.description: A compact simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with positive isotropic curvature is a homotopy sphere, hence homeomorphic to Sⁿ by the generalized Poincaré conjecture; the proof uses minimal two-spheres from the variational theory of the energy of maps S²→M and an index estimate from the second variation (Micallef–Moore 1988).

concept.title: Ricci flow with surgery
concept.description: A procedure that runs the Ricci flow until high-curvature regions form, cuts along nearly round necks, caps the pieces with standard caps and restarts the flow, with controlled surgery parameters. Introduced by Hamilton for four-manifolds with positive isotropic curvature and developed by Perelman in dimension three; Chen–Zhu completed the four-dimensional positive isotropic curvature case.

concept.title: Brendle–Schoen classification of manifolds with weakly 1/4-pinched curvature
concept.description: A compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise weakly 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures (0≤K(π₁)≤4K(π₂) at each point) is either diffeomorphic to a spherical space form or isometric to a locally symmetric space (Brendle–Schoen, Acta Math. 2008).

concept.title: Compact rank one symmetric space
concept.description: A compact Riemannian symmetric space of rank one: a round sphere, real, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley projective plane. With suitably normalized canonical metrics the complex, quaternionic and Cayley projective spaces have sectional curvatures ranging over [1,4] at every point.

concept.title: 2-positive curvature operator
concept.description: An algebraic curvature tensor (or a Riemannian manifold, at every point) has 2-positive curvature operator if the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of its curvature operator on ∧² is positive, and 2-nonnegative curvature operator if this sum is nonnegative.

concept.title: Nonnegativity of the trace of a product of positive semidefinite matrices
concept.description: If A and B are real symmetric positive semidefinite n×n matrices, then tr(AB)≥0.

concept.title: Induced inner product on the exterior square of a Euclidean space
concept.description: For a Euclidean space V, the inner product on ∧²V with ⟨x∧y,z∧w⟩=⟨x,z⟩⟨y,w⟩−⟨x,w⟩⟨y,z⟩, for which e_i∧e_j (i<j) is an orthonormal basis whenever (e_i) is.

Inspected all of Maehara’s three-page proof. Tietze extends the identity on an arc; pasting and radial/antipodal maps contradict Brouwer to show that each complementary component has the whole curve as boundary. Euclidean open sets are locally path connected, so their connected components are open and path connected; these elementary local facts are retained explicitly in the proof notes. No polygonal-approximation theorem is used on this route.

Complete dyadic-band proof: group radii in successive bands (2^(−k−1)R,2^(−k)R]. In each band take a maximal disjoint subfamily among balls avoiding earlier selected bands (Zorn). Every omitted ball meets a selected ball with at least half its radius, so it lies in that selected ball’s fivefold dilation. All selected balls are disjoint and the Euclidean rational dense subset makes the family countable. This proves the exact bounded-radii, possibly uncountable-family statement; it is not the distinct almost-everywhere Vitali covering theorem.

For any complex eigenpair(λ,z), choose i maximizing|z_i|/v_i to get|λ|≤r. Apply the same argument to Aᵀ for a positive left eigenvector. An eigenvector at r is a scalar multiple of v by subtracting an extremal coordinate ratio and propagating zero coordinates through irreducibility. The upcrossing bound on each finite ordered rational-time grid gives uniformly bounded expected upcrossings of any rational interval for a nonnegative martingale (equivalently apply the submartingale bound to its negative). Exhaust the nonnegative rational times by these grids; monotone convergence makes every rational interval have finitely many upcrossings almost surely. Thus rational-time limsup and liminf coincide; Fatou bounds the limiting expectation and excludes an infinite limit. Right-continuity extends convergence from rational times to all real times.

At first hitting a, the strong Markov property restarts an independent standard Brownian motion. Negating this future increment preserves its law by Gaussian symmetry. This path involution maps endpoint sets belowa to their reflected sets abovea, while keeping the event of first hittinga beforet fixed; endpoints above a necessarily hit a by continuity. Therefore the two terminal-event probabilities in the statement agree.

InspectedShenfeld–vanHandel§§1–3. First approximate by smooth positively curved bodies. The support-function integral formula, derived with divergence and change of variables, writes mixed volume as the quadratic form of a normalized symmetric elliptic operator. Its positive support-function eigenvector has eigenvalue1 and is the unique principal direction. Alexandrov’s mixed-discriminant inequality and symmetry of mixed volume give ∥Af∥²≥⟨f,Af⟩; the discrete spectral theorem then forces every other eigenvalue to be nonpositive. Reverse Cauchy–Schwarz for a form with one positive direction yields the desired mixed-volume inequality, and Hausdorff continuity removes smoothness. The matrix inequality is an immediate theorem prerequisite; its proof is not recursively followed.

concept_dependency.rationale: Complete directional facet-counting proof, alongsideTropp’s polytopal Cauchy exercise: for a polytope and a generic direction u, its visible facets project onto the interior of K|u⊥ with multiplicity one, and the hidden facets do the same. A facet’s projected area is its area times |u·ν|, so summing over all facets gives twice the projection volume. Continuity in u gives nongeneric directions. Approximate an arbitrary body by polytopes; projection-volume continuity passes the left side to the limit and weak continuity of area measure passes the continuous integrand |u·ν| on the right. This proves the directional identity, not merely the averaged surface-area formula.
concept_dependency.locator: ProblemSet2,problem3(f,g),and the complete directional argument in004-proof-notes.txt

concept_dependency.rationale: InspectedPapadimitrakis§§2.10–2.11 and5.9, specialized to the disk. The distribution−Δu/(2π) is a positive locally finite measure. Subtracting its logarithmic potential gives a harmonic distribution by Weyl’s lemma; harmonic correction replaces the local logarithmic kernel by the Green kernel on each concentric subdisk. The greatest harmonic minorant bounds these Green potentials; their monotone limit and Harnack convergence give u=Gμ+h. Distributional Laplacians give uniqueness of the measure, and harmonic minorants give uniqueness of h. Apply positive-harmonic Poisson representation to h for the boundary-measure clause. Concentric disk Green formulas supply the domain limit directly. We flatten the local/global forms of Riesz’s decomposition into this one theorem identity instead of creating a duplicate named theorem.

There are N!/(s!2ᵈd!) matchings with s monomers and d=(N−s)/2 dimers. Stirling, uniformly on a dense admissible grid with endpoint conventions0log0=0, gives the pressure as max_m[(h−J)m+Jm²−m logm−(1−m)log(1−m)/2−(1−m)/2]. A sum of at mostN+1 weights has logarithm between its maximum log weight and that maximum pluslog(N+1). The pure case gives p₀(z)=max_m[zm+entropy(m)], solved by m=g(z). Completing the square shows the stated maximum−Jr²+p₀(h−J+2Jr) equals this same pressure; forJ=0 it reduces to p₀(h).

Stop the diffusion inside a compact set and expand f along refining time partitions to first order in time and second order in space. Continuity makes the higher-order remainder bounded by a modulus tending to zero times the sum of squared increments. Brownian quadratic-covariation identifies the second-order sums with σσᵀdt; drift/noise cross terms vanish. Predictable first-order Brownian sums converge by Itô isometry to the stochastic integral, while time sums converge to their pathwise integrals. Localization removes the compact restriction and yields exactly the displayed formula.
concept_dependency.locator: Proof examined: localized second-order partition expansion

The diagonal ordered pairs contribute T_t(fg). Every off-diagonal ordered pair has a unique branching event where its two lineages first choose distinct children. Conditional on that event at(s,z), the mean product of the two independent descendant sums is(T_{t−s}f)(z)(T_{t−s}g)(z), and the expected number of ordered distinct-child choices isE[A(A−1)]. Compensating the rate-β branching events, then applying many-to-one to their ancestral positions, yields βE[A(A−1)]∫₀ᵗT_s[(T_{t−s}f)(T_{t−s}g)]ds. Nonnegative truncations justify Fubini and the finite-second-moment extension.

concept_dependency.rationale: Mark k lineages by independent uniform child choices under the original law. A given terminal k-tuple has conditional marking probability∏a_v^{-D(v)}. Write p_n for the law at n, c_n=min_xp_n(x)/π(x), and c_{−1}=0. Stationarity gives c_n≥c_{n−1}. Conditional on not having stopped before n, the unnormalized state mass is p_n−c_{n−1}π. Stop in statex with probability (c_n−c_{n−1})π(x)/(p_n(x)−c_{n−1}π(x)), using independent uniforms; interpret0/0 as0. The stopped mass at(n,x) is exactly(c_n−c_{n−1})π(x). Hence X_T is stationary and independent ofT, whileP(T>n)=1−c_n=sep(p_n,π); convergence to equilibrium ensuresT<∞ a.s. Conversely any strong stationary time has p_n(x)≥P(T≤n)π(x), giving its required tail lower bound.

Let p_n,q_n be the two marginal laws and ν_n=min(p_n,q_n) pointwise, ν_{−1}=0. Because ν_{n−1}P≤p_n,q_n, δ_n=ν_n−ν_{n−1}P is nonnegative. In each marginal chain independently define a killing rule that removes massδ_n at timen from its current unremoved state mass; the two rules have the same joint killing-time/location lawδ_n(x). Couple these time/location variables identically, sample the respective pre-killing paths conditional on them, and after killing use one common Markov future. On{T>n}, the marginal unremoved state masses are p_n−ν_n and q_n−ν_n, whose supports are disjoint, so the paths cannot have met. Thus T is their first meeting and coalescence time, withP(T>n)=1−∑_xν_n(x)=d_TV(p_n,q_n). Any residualT=∞ mass is coupled by its conditional path laws. This construction preserves each Markov marginal and need not be co-adapted.

concept_dependency.rationale: Take k with Pᵏ strictly positive. Perron–Frobenius gives a unique positive left eigenvectorπ of Pᵏ at eigenvalue1, normalized to sum1. Commutation and normalization implyπP=π. For a positive stochastic matrix, equality in the triangle bound for an eigenvector with|λ|=1 forces all coordinates to have the same complex phase and equal modulus, henceλ=1 and the vector constant. Thus all other eigenvalues ofPᵏ have modulus<1. Jordan normal form makes its nontrivial blocks tend to0, soP^{kn}→1π. Multiplying by finitely many remaining powers provesPⁿ→1π and the finite-state total variation conclusion.

Give D(E) its complete E₁ inner product and let J:D(E)→H be inclusion. Riesz gives the bounded adjoint, and T=JJ* is bounded, positive, injective and has dense range. Polar decomposition identifies Range(T¹ᐟ²)=Range(J)=D(E), with the E₁ norm represented by T^{-1/2}. Bounded self-adjoint spectral calculus defines A=T^{-1}−I and gives E(u,v)=⟨A¹ᐟ²u,A¹ᐟ²v⟩ onD(E). The same calculus defines the contractions e^{−tA}; dominated convergence gives strong continuity. Conversely, Hille–Yosida gives the generator of a strongly continuous self-adjoint contraction semigroup. Its Laplace-transform resolvent is self-adjoint, so its negative generator is nonnegative self-adjoint. Spectral resolution defines its closed square-root form and recovers the semigroup.

Lax–Milgram and Poincaré solve the coercive weak Dirichlet problem; the inverse maps L² boundedly intoH₀¹. Rellich makes its L² resolvent compact, while symmetry makes it self-adjoint and positivity makes its eigenvalues positive. The compact spectral theorem yields a complete eigenbasis and discrete unbounded generator eigenvalues. The strong maximum principle makes the Dirichlet resolvent positivity-improving. The compact positive-operator Perron theorem therefore gives a strictly positive principal eigenfunction and simplicity. Elliptic eigenfunction regularity gives the smooth interior/boundary statements. Spectral calculus gives the semigroup expansion.

concept_dependency.rationale: The closed form E(u,v)=½∫∇u·∇v has domainH₀¹: completeness follows from Sobolev completeness and Poincaré. Its associated self-adjoint operator is the weak Dirichlet−½Δ by the form’s defining variational identity. The same spectral calculus givesD(A) by the squared-eigenvalue sum; by the weak operator definition this is exactly weakΔf∈L² with zero trace. Thus finite eigenfunction sums are dense in the form norm as well asL², with no unproved upgrade fromL² density or globalH² claim onC¹ boundaries.

concept_dependency.rationale: For tight M choose increasing compactsK_m with mass≥1−2^{-m}. Compact-space weak compactness and a diagonal subsequence give weak limits of all restricted measures μ_n|K_m; these limits increase as measures and have mass tending to1. Their monotone limitμ is a probability measure, and the compact restrictions plus the uniform tail bound show μ_n(f)→μ(f) for every bounded continuousf. Conversely, tightness from small neighborhoods of compacts follows by intersecting compact neighborhoods at radiiε2^{-m}, obtaining a closed totally bounded subset of the complete space. If M is not tight, the contrapositive produces a fixedε>0 and successively separated compact setsK_n carrying definite mass for selectedμ_n while later K’s carry little mass for earlierμ_n. Uniformly Lipschitz cutoffs on their disjointε/2-neighborhoods can be assigned signs recursively so the resulting bounded continuous test function has nonconvergent μ_n integrals on every subsequence. Thus M cannot be weakly precompact.

Induct simultaneously on vertex count that μ_G is real-rooted and μ_{G−u} weakly interlacesμ_G. WithH=G−u, deletion givesR=μ_G/μ_H=z−∑_{v∼u}w_uv μ_{H−v}/μ_H. Inductive interlacing and the positive-partial-fraction lemma express each quotient as∑c_j/(z−r_j),c_j≥0, after common-factor cancellation. ThusImR(z)>0 wheneverImz>0, soμ_G has no upper-half-plane zeros; real coefficients exclude lower-half-plane zeros. On the real line R′=1+∑wc_j/(x−r_j)²>0 between its poles, giving interlacing of the reduced numerator and denominator. Reinserting common factors preserves weak interlacing: a pole drops a denominator multiplicity by one, a regular shared root retains it, and a regular zero can raise it by one. Zero weights/residues are omitted. The empty and single-vertex bases are immediate.

Nonnegative boundary lower limits force any negative sublevel set to lie in a compact subset of the bounded domain. Lower semicontinuity attains a negative minimum there. The super-mean inequality forces equality to that minimum on each sufficiently small circle around a minimum point: if a point on a circle were larger, lower semicontinuity would make its mean larger. Thus the minimum set is both open and closed in its component. A negative constant contradicts the boundary condition. The same argument proves the interior-minimum assertion.

concept_dependency.rationale: Difference quotients of the solution satisfy linear SDEs with bounded derivative coefficients. BDG and Grönwall show convergence to the Jacobian equation, moment bounds, and spatial increment bounds; induction gives all higher derivatives. Kolmogorov’s criterion on compact parameter sets supplies a common smooth version. The inverse Jacobian solves dK=−KDV₀dt−ΣKDV_i∘dB^i, and the Stratonovich product rule gives KJ=I. For fixed terminal time the backward Stratonovich equation, driven by the reversed Brownian increments, has bounded smooth coefficients and a global solution; pathwise uniqueness and the flow property identify it as the two-sided inverse of x↦X_t^x. This establishes global bijectivity as well as local invertibility, rather than deducing the former merely from detJ≠0. Linear derivative equations and BDG/Grönwall give every finite moment of derivatives and inverse Jacobians, uniformly in x on bounded times.

concept_dependency.rationale: Write F(m)=−Jm²+p₀((2m−1)J+h) and g=p₀′. Then F′=2J(g−m), F″=−2J+(2J)²g′. The explicit monotone inverse g⁻¹(u)=logu−½log(1−u) reduces the sign of g′−1/(2J) to a quadratic inequality, giving the exact J_c and two inflection branches for J>J_c. Hence there are at most two local maxima; stationary branches vary smoothly when F″≠0 by the implicit-function theorem. In the two-maxima strip, their height difference Δ has derivative ∂_hΔ=m₂−m₁>0, and opposite signs at the two strip endpoints. The intermediate-value theorem gives a unique coexistence field γ(J); the implicit-function theorem makes it smooth. The critical endpoint is where the two inflections coalesce: substitution gives m_c,J_c,h_c and F″=F‴=0,F⁽⁴⁾<0. Away from it, a degenerate stationary point is a spinodal inflection, not a global maximum, so the retained global maximizers are nondegenerate. The underlying paper has apparent reversed sign typos in the prose of Proposition4’s proof; the displayed derivative(33) and this calculation fix the direction.

Ehrling’s inequality follows by contradiction: normalize ‖v_n‖_X=1 with bounded X₀ norm and X₁ norm→0, then use compactness X₀→X and injectivity X→X₁. For the time-dependent family, the weak derivative bound gives ‖u(t+h)−u(t)‖_{X₁}≤h^{1−1/q}‖u′‖_{L^q(X₁)} by the Banach-valued fundamental theorem and Hölder. Ehrling and the Lᵖ(X₀) bound make time translates uniformly small in Lᵖ(X), first fixing ε then h. Replace each u by its averages on a finite equal time partition; the translate estimate makes this replacement uniformly small in Lᵖ(X). For each fixed partition, every average lies in a bounded subset of X₀ and therefore in a relatively compact subset of X. The finite products of their finite nets prove total boundedness, hence relative compactness in the complete Lᵖ(X) space. This proves the actual Lᵖ conclusion; bounds asserted in the synchronization paper do not by this theorem alone imply convergence in C([0,T];H⁻¹).

Flatten C¹,¹ boundary charts, freeze the principal coefficients on small balls, and absorb their oscillation times ‖D²u‖_p. Lemma2.4 reduces the question to a normalized suppression-unconditional spreading basis. Suppression1 gives a bounded sign-unconditionality constant (at most2 over the reals, and a harmless finite constant over the complexes); absorb it intoδ before taking positive coefficients and positive coordinate functionals. If small-coefficient ℓ¹-normalized positive combinations keep norm≥δ, choose finite positive norming coordinate functionals with uniformly bounded norm. At least a fixed amount of pairing occurs on coordinates with functional coefficient≥δ/4; their number grows because max a_i→0. Subsymmetry then bounds the norm of arbitrarily long sums of dual coordinate functionals uniformly. Hence that dual sequence is c₀-equivalent, forcing the original basis ℓ¹-equivalent, a contradiction. The converse is immediate from anℓ¹ lower estimate. Hahn–Banach supplies the norming functionals.

Inspected TaoTheorem1.6.40 andExercises1.6.48–51. An L¹ primitive is absolutely continuous by truncating its integrand, and has derivative equal to that integrand at Lebesgue points. Conversely absolute continuity implies bounded variation; Jordan decomposition and monotone differentiability give an integrable derivative. Cover the exceptional null set by an open set of arbitrarily small measure. Choose a gauge using differentiability and Lebesgue points elsewhere; Cousin gives a tagged partition. Telescope the increments, control exceptional intervals by absolute continuity and the L¹ small-set bound, and control all other intervals by derivative and integral averages. Let the error tend to zero, giving every endpoint increment.

On each rectangle compactly contained inΩ, use product test functions and Fubini in the weak derivative identity. A countable dense collection of one-dimensional tests gives, on almost every coordinate line, the one-dimensional weak identity. Subtract the indefinite integral of that slice’s L¹ derivative: its distributional derivative is zero, hence it is constant and the slice has an absolutely continuous representative. A countable rectangular cover gives the local slice assertion. Conversely, integrate by parts on the absolutely continuous slices and then apply Fubini; the Lp partials are weak derivatives. For continuous homeomorphisms, equality almost everywhere on each good slice identifies this representative with the given restriction.

Choose shifted dyadic partitions at times where X lies inV so that left- and right-step approximations converge in Lᵖ(V); density, translation continuity and Fubini supply a common deterministic sequence. Telescope the Hilbert norm square at partition points, pairing drift increments inV*×V and retaining martingale increment squares. BDG gives a uniform expected supremum norm bound. Finite-dimensional orthogonal projections and the Hilbert Itô isometry make the stochastic sums converge uniformly in probability. Drift pairings converge by Lᵖ–L^{p′} duality. The remaining nonnegative squared drift-increment error is bounded by its square root times the martingale tail’s quadratic variation; Parseval sends that tail to zero. The formula first holds on the countable partition union. It then gives Cauchy convergence inH at arbitrary times; weakH continuity plus continuity of the norm yields strongH continuity and extends the identity simultaneously to all times. No assumption that the noise is V-valued is used.

For V=L^{m+1}(Ω),H=H⁻¹, the porous drift has dual pairing ⟨Δu[m],v⟩=−∫u[m]v. Its scalar power is monotone and uniformly p-monotone, and Young’s inequality gives the required growth/coercivity bounds. Construct a strictly stationary continuousH, locallyLp(V) solution Z of the strongly monotone equation with driftΔu[m] and the same noise. Subtract Z; pathwise Y=X−Z solves a deterministic monotone evolution equation, with coefficients shifted byZ and integrable coercivity/growth bounds. The deterministic theorem gives a solution for every initial state on one invariant noise set, and Grönwall gives continuity in the initial state. Uniqueness supplies the flow law; strict stationarity of Z and time independence of the drift give the cocycle law after addingZ back. This is why subtracting a merely H-valued Brownian path directly is insufficient: the stationary porous solution has the needed localLp(V) regularity.
concept_dependency.locator: Gess2012Theorem2.5 and§4.3 proof, additive autonomous specialization

concept_dependency.rationale: Add to the second copy a coupling drift β_t(X−Y)/‖X−Y‖^ε until meeting, with ε=(σ+2−p)/(σ+2)>0. Monotonicity and the covariance-norm hypothesis bound its Cameron–Martin control energy and force meeting by the chosen time. Cylindrical Girsanov removes that drift; Hölder gives the dimension-free power Harnack inequality. Its cost vanishes as the initial states coalesce, so uniform integrability of the likelihood gives strong Feller continuity inL¹ (uniform integrability, not a bare dominated-convergence assertion). The energy formula and coercivity give tight occupation laws inH; compactness V→H follows by the adjoint ofH₀¹→L² and the bounded-domain inclusionLp→L². Krylov–Bogoliubov yields an invariant law. The Harnack inequality and path continuity give full support, then irreducibility; Doob’s theorem yields total-variation mixing. The R density uses the usual negative stochastic-integral sign when the shifted noise is W+∫h; sign typos in an intermediate printed density do not alter the stated theorem.

Use the two-sided Wiener representation and its fractional-integral inverse to track how a change of the noise past affects future increments. Dissipativity gives a Lyapunov moment bound and contracts the distance under common increments. On a bounded-distance, bounded-memory-cost set, add a feedback drift to make the trajectories coincide by time1; the inverse fractional transform has uniformly bounded Wiener L² control energy. Girsanov bounds the common mass of the shifted and original Wiener laws, permitting a positive-probability coupling attempt. Meeting is not by itself permanent, since the fractional noise remembers the differing past. The explicit kernel estimates in Lemma5.12 give continuation success probabilities on doubling intervals at least1−K2^{−αN}. Their infinite product is positive. After failure, wait long enough for the weighted memory cost to decrease, as Lemma5.15 proves; this permits another attempt with a uniform chance of permanent success. Section6 bounds the finite retry durations by a polynomially weighted geometric sum with power-tail increments; its tail tends to zero. Thus the probability that the two future trajectories differ tends to zero, and the coupling inequality gives total-variation convergence. Tightness/Lyapunov bounds yield a stationary law with the fixed Gaussian noise marginal. The ordinary H=½ case, excluded from this theorem’s paragraph, is covered separately; no future-dependent stationary solutions are asserted unique.

Order the events. For A_i let B_i be the event that none of its preceding coordinate-disjoint events occur, and let Δ_i sum P(A_i∩A_j) over preceding coordinate-overlapping j. A_i is independent ofB_i. Since A_i∩A_j is increasing and B_i decreasing, Harris gives P(A_i∩A_j∩B_i)≤P(A_i∩A_j)P(B_i). Subtracting these overlaps gives P(A_i and no preceding events)≥(p_i−Δ_i)P(B_i). The probability of no preceding events is at mostP(B_i), so the conditional hazard is≥p_i−Δ_i whenever this is nonnegative, and trivially so otherwise. Thus each conditional avoidance probability is≤1−p_i+Δ_i. Multiplying, using1−x≤e^{−x}, yields exp(−μ+Δ). Alternatively factor1−p_i and bound1+Δ_i/(1−p_i)≤exp(Δ_i/(1−ε)); this gives the product form. A zero preceding-avoidance probability already proves the conclusion.

At each fixed radius, the degree bound and finite mark alphabet permit only finitely many rooted ball types. Successive subsequence extraction and a diagonal subsequence make each ball type eventually constant. Choose compatible representatives inductively and take their increasing union to obtain the rooted limit, retaining full degree/port marks when present. The distance2^{−R}, whereR is the largest agreeing radius, with distance1 if the radius-zero marks disagree and distance0 for agreement at all radii, metrizes local convergence. A Cauchy sequence has stabilizing balls at every radius, so the same union proves completeness. Finitely many ball types give finite covers at each radius, hence total boundedness and compactness; their representatives also give separability. This applies to the paper’s factor templates because all type, weight and port alphabets are finite.

Detailed balance conjugates P bydiag(√π) to a real symmetric tridiagonal matrix with strictly positive off-diagonal entries. Its orthonormal eigenbasis and simple spectrum give a discrete spectral measure at the first basis vector. The first coordinate of each eigenvector is nonzero: if it vanished, the tridiagonal eigenvalue equation recursively forces every coordinate to vanish. The same recurrence identifies all other coordinates as√(π(x)/π(0))φ_x(λ) times the first coordinate. Assign mass equal to that first coordinate’s square at each eigenvalue. Orthonormal completeness gives the polynomial orthogonality, and the spectral expansion ofPⁿ gives the stated transition formula. A stochastic matrix’s real eigenvalues lie in[−1,1].
concept_dependency.locator: Coquio2015Appendix§5.1 equations(28)–(29); direct checked finite-matrix proof

The intermediate-value theorem supplies a zero in every intervening interval. The monic leading-term signs give one further zero beyond each extreme zero ofp_n. Degree counting accounts for exactlyn+1 distinct real zeros, proving strict interlacing. All denominator norms through p_n stay positive. For exactly n+1 support points, the constructed p_{n+1} is orthogonal to every degree≤n polynomial, so it vanishes at every support point and is their monic product; its own norm can be zero and is never divided by.

For a compactly supported Lipschitz u, near-diagonal radial integration is bounded by a compact integral of(2−α)⁻¹. The far part with one variable in the support is bounded by compact integrals ofα⁻¹ and the assumed outside integral of|x|^{−d−α(x)}. Thus the core energy is finite. The maximal difference-operator form is closed: from anL²-Cauchy/energy-Cauchy sequence extract an almost-everywhere subsequence using Chebyshev/Borel–Cantelli; the differences then converge pointwise for the jump measure, whileL² completeness and Fatou identify the energy limit. Restricting that closed form to the core gives closability. Unit truncation preserves the compact Lipschitz core and decreases every squared difference, so the closure is Markovian. Continuous compact functions areL²-dense by bounded clipping of theirL¹ approximations, and mollification approximates them uniformly by compactly supported Lipschitz functions. Use a Borel isomorphism to put the target in a Borel subsetB of[0,1]. For every rationalq choose conditional expectations of1_{X≤q}, obtained by Radon–Nikodym onG. Outside one null set for the countably many rational comparisons, these are nondecreasing; conditional monotone convergence supplies rational right limits. Extend them right-continuously to a distribution function with limits0,1 and use the Lebesgue–Stieltjes theorem to obtain a probability kernel. Measurability first holds on half-lines and extends to every Borel set by the pi–lambda theorem, which also extends the conditional-integral identity. The conditional probability ofBᶜ has expectation0, so after changing one null set the kernel is supported onB; transport it back toE. Uniqueness on a countable generating pi-system gives one common null set, rather than a different null set for every Borel set. The product-measure disintegration follows by conditioning on the first-coordinate sigma-algebra.

Choose increasing compactE_m with mean mass≥1−2^{−m} for every kernel. At eachm choose a countable dense rational-linear test family inC(E_m), including constants, and consider all restricted kernel test integrals. These countably many random variables, for alln,m, generate a countably generated sub-sigma-algebraG. ItsL¹ is separable modulo null sets. Banach–Alaoglu andL¹/L∞ duality give a common diagonal weak-* subsequence for the test integrals onG. Positivity, linearity and mass≤1 pass to the limit outside a single null set by countability. Riesz–Markov yields measurable positive subprobability kernelsν_m supported onE_m. Comparing nonnegative tests on larger compacts givesν_m≤ν_{m+1}. Their increasing limit has mass≤1; its expected mass tends to1 by the uniform mean tail bound, so it is a probability kernel almost surely. Stable convergence first holds on each compact restriction. Uniform mean tails control the error by2^{−m} times the bounded test norms, proving it onE. For an arbitrary boundedF-measurable base testa, replace it byE[a|G] in all pairings; this extends convergence beyondG. This avoids falsely assuming the original base sigma-algebra is countably generated or applying sequential Banach–Alaoglu on a nonseparableL¹.
concept_dependency.locator: Synchronization2015Lemma2.5 compactness input credited toCrauel; checked compact-restriction/weak-* proof

Approximate the subdifferential by the Lipschitz gradients of its Moreau–Yosida envelopes and solve the resulting equations after subtracting the fixed continuous driver, using ordinary Picard–Lindelöf. An interior ball in dom∂η gives the coercive graph estimate⟨a(x),x−x₀⟩≥r|a(x)|−C(1+|x|). Subdivide time so the driver oscillation is smaller thanr; in the integration-by-parts estimate the driver–correction term is absorbed into the left-hand variation bound. This yields local uniform state/variation bounds depending on the driver modulus, not its total variation. Parametrize by elapsed time plus accumulated correction variation; the corrections then are uniformly Lipschitz. Helly and Arzelà–Ascoli give a convergent subsequence. The graph inequality identifies the limit: on a flat physical-clock interval the driver and drift integral are constant, so y_r−y_s=−(K_r−K_s). Extend the graph inequality in its fixed state argument to closure(dom∂η) and choose y_s. The continuous bounded-variation quadratic identity gives ∫⟨y_r−y_s,dK_r⟩=−|K_t−K_s|²/2≥0, hence K and y are constant on every such subinterval. The monotone-clock uniform-convergence criterion now permits undoing the clock. Its elementary proof bounds inverse clocks on a compact interval, extracts s_n with τ_n(s_n)=t_n, and uses τ(s)=t and constancy on its level interval; sequential compactness makes convergence uniform. Pass the variational inequalities using the bounded-variation integral limit. For two solutions with the same driver, testing the two graph inequalities against resolvent-regularized averages gives∫⟨X−Y,dK−dL⟩≥0; Grönwall yields uniqueness and continuity in the initial state. The same bounds applied to converging drivers give continuous dependence. Since the construction is pathwise for all continuous inputs and the drift is autonomous, uniqueness gives the flow and shift-cocycle laws without an input-dependent exceptional set. The earlier1995 primary scan supplies the resolvent, monotonicity and time-change identification mechanism; the full1998 printed proof was not accessible, so this deterministic route is explicitly curator-written.

On the open interval whereη is finite, its subgradient is locally bounded and equalsη′ except at a countable set. Since the Brownian part has quadratic variationt, the occupation-time formula makes that exceptional set irrelevant to the time drift. Thus the interior diffusion generator is½f″+(b−η′)f′. Its speed density is a constant multiple ofexp(2∫b−2η). Convexity boundsη below by an affine function, and b has bounded primitive on the bounded domain, so the speed measure has finite nonzero mass. Pathwise well-posedness gives a conservative solution; nondegenerate unit Brownian noise makes the interior regular and irreducible. The subgradient boundary correction is instantaneous normal reflection at a regular finite endpoint, or the singular potential makes the endpoint inaccessible; it cannot give absorbing or sticky holding with unit quadratic variation. The finite-speed-measure theorem gives the invariant density and total-variation convergence. This checks the exact one-dimensional application without claiming to have read the unavailable fullCépa–Jacquot primary proof.

Subtract the continuous Brownian path to solve a locally Lipschitz time-dependent ODE up to explosion. Apply Itô to the stopped square: the drift bound gives uniform finite-time second-moment bounds, so the exit probabilities tend to zero and the solution is nonexplosive. Dividing xb(x)≤C−cx² byx on the positive and negative tails and integrating in the proper direction shows∫₀^x b(s)ds≤−c′x²+C′log(2+|x|)+C″. Thus the speed densityexp(2∫b) is integrable. Unit Brownian diffusion is regular and irreducible, and the finite-speed-measure theorem gives the unique stationary law and total-variation mixing. The source’s stronger two-point dissipativity condition implies this one-point bound after fixingy=0, so this covers itsH=½ case.

Apply the cube regularity theorem at a smaller δ. Its homogeneous state classes have small empirical-spin fluctuations. Lemma2.8 turns regularity plus small fluctuations into average k-coordinate independence: Markov bounds conditional marginal discrepancies on every event of mass above a small threshold, then conditioning sequentially on k spins and telescoping the joint/product difference bounds its expectation. The negligible small conditional events contribute at most their probability; repeated coordinate choices cost O(k²/n). Discard irregular state classes and those of mass below η=ε/(2N); their total mass is below ε. The remaining conditional laws satisfy the requested independence. This is an independently reusable consequence, distinct from the empirical-distribution statement of the regularity theorem.

The mean laws converge weakly and hence form a tight family. Truncate the integrable random envelope, then choose a compact K with uniformly small mean mass outside it. On K approximate F by a finite deterministic continuous partition of unity at a δ-net, with random coefficients F(ω,x_j). Metric bump functions, normalized using the distance to K as an extra outside weight, provide bounded globally continuous weights. For each ω its continuous restriction to K is uniformly continuous, so the expected uniform approximation error tends to zero by dominated convergence. Stable convergence applies to each random coefficient times a deterministic weight. The outside-K bound and envelope truncation complete the argument. This supplies the random-composed-test step in the invariant measure proof without assuming it in the definition of stable convergence.

Subtract the continuous stochastic heat convolution Z. Penalize the lower and upper violations, using the one-wall construction first and then removing the other penalty monotonically. For a smooth approximating free field, the double-obstacle variational theorem gives the deterministic limit. The uniform supremum stability estimate, proved by testing the positive part after shifting by the sup norm of the driver difference and applying an exponential drift adjustment, transfers existence/continuity to the actual continuous Z. Smooth periodic approximations of the H² walls preserve their strictly positive gap; their second derivatives converge inL². Positive limiting reflection distributions are Radon measures. Strict separation of the two compact contact sets permits separate smooth test cutoffs, giving finite reflection masses on compact time intervals; the uniform state limit and weak measure limits give complementarity. For equal noise, the difference equation has no stochastic term; its reflection pairing is nonpositive, so energy testing and Grönwall give uniqueness. The same stability gives continuity in the initial state. Autonomous pathwise construction and the two-time heat-convolution identity give the cocycle on a common noise set. Otobe prints interval boundary conditions; replacing the interval by periodic integration removes the boundary terms in each maximum-principle/energy argument, and the cited periodic primary confirms the H² assumptions. The source’s displayed transformed f(Y−Z) is corrected to f(Y+Z).

Until hitting0, Itô applied toY=2√X yields Y≤Y₀+B; Brownian hitting−2√B by clock time c_TT gives a uniform positive chance p of meeting. Stick together after meeting. Choose a countable dense family of test functions inL^{p′}. Uniform Lp boundedness and Hölder bound all their pairings; successive Bolzano–Weierstrass extraction and the diagonal sequence make every such pairing converge. The dual representation of the Lp norm as a supremum of unit-test pairings gives the lower bound; first choose a subsequence realizing the original liminf if that version is required.

Approximate Z strongly inL^{m+1}(time×space) andC(H⁻¹), smoothing ordered initial data by powers of the Dirichlet resolvent. For each smooth approximation, addingZ back yields a deterministic porous equation with the same smooth forcing for both initial states; the forced inverse-potential comparison applies. To justify passage to the limit, let X_n=Y_n+Z_n. In the H⁻¹ difference energy identity the leading term is−2∫(Φ(X_n)−Φ(X_k))(X_n−X_k)≤−C‖X_n−X_k‖_p^p. Uniform energy bounds and Hölder make their time integrals vanish, since Φ:Lp→L^{p′} is continuous by the scalar mean-value bound. The linear reaction contributes at most C‖Y_n−Y_k‖_H²+C‖Z_n−Z_k‖_H². BoundedR and the closed positive cone pass the order; continuous dependence extends from a dense set of ordered data.

Complete directional facet-counting proof, alongsideTropp’s polytopal Cauchy exercise: for a polytope and a generic direction u, its visible facets project onto the interior of K|u⊥ with multiplicity one, and the hidden facets do the same. A facet’s projected area is its area times |u·ν|, so summing over all facets gives twice the projection volume. Continuity in u gives nongeneric directions. Approximate an arbitrary body by polytopes; projection-volume continuity passes the left side to the limit and weak continuity of area measure passes the continuous integrand |u·ν| on the right. This proves the directional identity, not merely the averaged surface-area formula.

concept_dependency.rationale: The definition tests the base changes X×_k Spec K to field extensions, in particular to an algebraic closure.
Each base change is required to be a reduced scheme.
The statement concerns an algebraic group G over a field, with identity point e.
Tgt_e(G) is the Zariski tangent space at the rational point e; the proof identifies it with Hom_k(𝔪_e/𝔪_e²,k) (A.51).
