concept_dependency.rationale: The inequality compares with dim G, the dimension of the finite-type scheme G.
dim Tgt_e(G) is the dimension of a finite-dimensional k-vector space.
Equality is characterized as smoothness of G over k.
A.49/A.52: dim O ≤ dim 𝔪/𝔪² with equality exactly when O_(G,e) is regular.
A.49 uses that the Krull dimension of a Noetherian local ring is at most the number of generators of its maximal ideal (A.45, Krull).
A.49: by Nakayama’s lemma elements of 𝔪 generate 𝔪 iff they span 𝔪/𝔪², so the minimal number of generators is dim 𝔪/𝔪².
A.52 compares dim Tgt_e with dim X through dim O_(X,e)=dim X for an irreducible algebraic scheme at a closed point (A.47).
A.52 is applied on the irreducible component through e (1.35), whose dimension is dim G because all components have the same dimension.
The component through e is the identity component G°, an open subgroup with dim G°=dim G.
Over k^a a rational point is smooth exactly when its local ring is regular, and a finite-type scheme over the perfect field k^a is smooth iff all local rings are regular (A.54, smooth ⇒ regular).
Milne defines smoothness over k through G_(k^a); smoothness of G gives smoothness of G_(k^a).
Conversely smoothness of G_(k^a) descends to G along the faithfully flat Spec k^a→Spec k, matching Milne’s definition with smoothness of G→Spec k.
Proposition 1.28 (b)⇒(a): after translating e to every closed point of G_(k^a) (1.8), the smooth locus is an open set containing all closed points.

concept_dependency.rationale: Irreducibility is defined for elements of an integral domain.
The definition excludes units and requires one factor of any factorization to be a unit.
A prime element is a nonunit dividing a factor whenever it divides a product.

A UFD is an integral domain in which nonzero nonunits factor into irreducible elements uniquely up to order and units.
The recorded characterization: given existence of factorizations, uniqueness is equivalent to every irreducible element generating a prime ideal.

Statement: the hypothesis on S⁻¹A and the conclusion on A are unique factorization. Proof: in the UFD S⁻¹A an irreducible image is prime, and the final step concludes via the criterion that factorizations plus irreducibles prime give a UFD (Lemma 10.120.5, recorded in the UFD paragraph).

Statement: the hypothesis. Proof: the union of an ascending chain of principal ideals is an ideal, hence principal, so the chain stabilizes; and the maximal ideal containing (a) is principal.
Statement: the conclusion. Proof: Theorem 2.6.6(3), factorizations plus every irreducible prime gives a UFD, recorded as the characterization in the UFD paragraph.
Statement: irreducible elements generate maximal ideals. Proof: (a) lies in a maximal ideal I=(b), and b|a with b a nonunit forces (a)=I.
Having shown the ascending chain condition on principal ideals, the proof concludes existence of factorizations into irreducibles from Theorem 2.6.6(2).

source.title: Manifolds with 1/4-pinched curvature are space forms
source.coverage: Read in full: the published version of record (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 22 (2009) 287-307, PDF sha256 1f099f9a...c877, via text extracted with page markers), every section (§1 Introduction with Theorems 1-3; §2 Lemma 4 to Proposition 11 with all proofs; §3 Propositions 12-17 and Theorem 18; §4 Lemmas 19-20, Proposition 21, Corollary 22 with proofs), the front matter (received date, MSC, keywords, grant acknowledgements in the first-page footnote; there is no separate acknowledgements section and no appendix) and all 29 references. The arXiv v3 LaTeX source (sha256 9924...2954) was read alongside for formulas, and a word-level diff of the v3 PDF text against the VOR text (scratch/v3-vs-vor-worddiff.txt) found only layout, hyphenation and ligature differences plus VOR-only MR numbers, received date, MSC and keywords; the v3 source also contains a commented-out abstract and a commented-out proof of Proposition 15 not printed in either version. Final reconciliation additionally used the attribution reviewer's downloads (output/predecessors/): arXiv v1 (2007-05-06) and v2 (2007-05-22) of this paper (checked for earliest appearance of each claimed result and credit), Böhm–Wilking arXiv:math/0606187 (Theorem 2, §3 definition, Prop. 3.2, Lemmas 3.4-3.5, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 read directly), Nguyen's ANU thesis (title page, abstract, Theorem 4.8), Ni–Wolfson arXiv:0706.0332 (§§1-3, §5 read directly), Yau–Zheng 1991 pp. 529-531 (page images) and the zbMATH record of Chen 1991. Not inspected: Hamilton 1986, Chen 1991 full text, Micallef–Moore, Andrews–Nguyen, Grove–Karcher–Ruh, Im Hof–Ruh, Sampson, the Annals version of Böhm–Wilking. The long component calculations in Propositions 5-9 were followed but not independently re-derived.
source.summary: The paper proves the differentiable 1/4-pinched sphere theorem: a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures admits a constant curvature metric and is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form (Theorem 1), with an equivariant version (Theorem 2). Both follow from a convergence theorem for the normalized Ricci flow (Theorem 3 = Theorem 18) under the condition that the curvature tensor extended by zero to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has positive isotropic curvature margin (strict PIC2). The route is: (§2) nonnegative isotropic curvature is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R) in all dimensions (Proposition 11), proved via first and second variation identities at a minimizing orthonormal four-frame (Lemma 4 to Corollary 10), so by Hamilton's maximum principle PIC is preserved by the Ricci flow; (§3) applying this on ℝⁿ×ℝ² shows the cone Ĉ is ODE-invariant, contains nonnegative curvature operators and lies in nonnegative sectional curvature (Proposition 12), so the Böhm–Wilking deformation ℓ_{a,b} yields a pinching family (Propositions 13-15), from which a pinching set is built (Propositions 16-17, a new proof of Böhm–Wilking Theorem 4.1) and Hamilton/Böhm–Wilking convergence gives Theorem 18; (§4) an algebraic λμ-criterion for Ĉ (Proposition 21, via Lemmas 19-20) and Berger's inequality show 1/4-pinched curvature lies in Ĉ (Corollary 22).
source.dependency_review: The argument needs Riemannian curvature basics (curvature tensor with the first Bianchi identity, algebraic curvature tensors, sectional, Ricci and scalar curvature, curvature operator), isotropic curvature, the Ricci flow and normalized flow, Hamilton's curvature evolution equation and ODE, Hamilton's maximum principle (1986, Theorem 4.3), standard existence/uniqueness of Ricci flow, the Böhm–Wilking machinery (ℓ_{a,b} and their Theorem 2, the nonnegative-cone deformation Lemmas 3.4-3.5 whose proofs are asserted to carry over to Ĉ, pinching families, Theorem 5.1) and Hamilton's pinching-set convergence argument, all imported without proof; Berger's inequality; and elementary tools: ODE existence and continuous dependence, first- and second-derivative tests, positive semidefinite matrices, traces and tr(AB)≥0, the inner product on two-vectors, convex cones and tangent cones, exterior two-vectors, self-duality in dimension four, normal form of skew forms and the singular value decomposition. Deducing Theorems 1-2 also uses the Killing–Hopf classification and compact Lie group actions by isometries. Propositions 13-15 and Theorem 18 are not proved in the paper beyond citing [3] and [12].

source_concept.introduction_evidence: VOR p.287: 'This conjecture is known as the Differentiable Sphere Theorem, and the purpose of this paper is to prove this'. Present from arXiv v1 (2007-05-06), Theorem 1. Earlier differentiable sphere theorems credited (p.288) need global pinching δ ≥ 0.76 or pointwise pinching tending to 1 (Ruh). n=4: VOR p.288 credits H. Chen [6] ('which implies Theorem 1 for n = 4'); zbMATH review of Chen (Zbl 0752.53021, W. Ballmann): 'a compact pointwise 1/4-pinched 4-manifold is either diffeomorphic to the sphere or real projective space or isometric to the complex projective plane'. v1 instead attributed n=4 to Hamilton's PIC surgery work [10] with Chen-Zhu; v2 (2007-05-22) added 'Theorem 1 was proven in the case n = 4 by H. Chen [4]'. Nguyen's thesis (Jan 2008) proves only PIC preservation (Theorem 4.8) and contains no sphere theorem. Ni-Wolfson (arXiv 0706.0332, June 2007) give 'a different proof of the result of Brendle-Schoen' and call it 'Brendle-Schoen's recent differential sphere theorem'. Andrews-Nguyen is four-dimensional (not accessed).

source_concept.locator: pp. 287-288, Theorem 2; first appears in arXiv v2 (2007-05-22)
source_concept.note: Absent from v1.
source_concept.introduction_evidence: VOR p.288: 'Since our method of proof gives a canonical deformation from the 1/4-pinched metric to a constant curvature metric, we can also prove the following equivariant version.' Earlier equivariant results credited only under global δ-pinching: 'first proven for globally δ-pinched manifolds by K. Grove, H. Karcher, and E. Ruh [9], [10] ... (δ = 0.98). The pinching constant was later improved by H. Im Hof and E. Ruh [16].' v1 has no equivariant statement; v2 Theorem 2 introduces it. No earlier pointwise-1/4 equivariant result found in the inspected predecessors (BW, Nguyen thesis, Ni-Wolfson).

source_concept.introduction_evidence: VOR p.289: 'we establish a convergence result for the Ricci flow in dimension n ≥ 4 under a curvature condition which is substantially stronger than positive isotropic curvature, but includes the pointwise 1/4-pinched manifolds.' v1 Theorem 17 (2007-05-06): curvature in the interior of C-hat ⇒ normalized Ricci flow converges to constant curvature (proof via Cor. 16 and BW Thm 5.1). Mechanism credited to BW [3] and Hamilton [12]; the theorem for C-hat is not credited elsewhere. Ni-Wolfson (June 2007) attribute it to BS ('The consequence is the recent important result of Brendle and Schoen', Cor. 3.3) and reprove it via complex sectional curvature. Nguyen's thesis has no product cones or convergence theorem for them.

source_concept.introduction_evidence: VOR p.289: 'In Section 2 we prove that positive isotropic curvature is preserved by the Ricci flow in all dimensions'; 'In dimension 4, it was shown by R. Hamilton [14]'; 'After this paper was written, we learned that H. Nguyen [22] has independently proved that positive isotropic curvature is preserved under the Ricci flow.' v1 (2007-05-06) p.2 already says: 'We have learned that H. Nguyen has independently proved that PIC is preserved under the Ricci flow in his PhD dissertation.' Nguyen thesis (title page January 2008, ANU hdl 1885/150367) abstract: 'We illustrate these ideas by showing that non-negative isotropic curvature is preserved by the Ricci flow in all dimensions'; Theorem 4.8; its body reproves Hamilton's n=4 case and cites [BS] only in the bibliography (OCR). Thus R̃ is the curvature tensor one obtains for the manifold M × R. The condition that R̃ has positive isotropic curvature ... is a much stronger condition than positive isotropic curvature itself.' concept_formalization.evidence: Inspected upstream Mathlib commit 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. Group at Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean:33 extends DivInvMonoid with left inverse cancellation; mul_inv_cancel at :62 proves right inverse cancellation, and toCancelMonoid at :102 proves cancellation, matching the catalogue group definition. AddGroup (:44) is the same mathematical structure in additive notation. Basic.lean supplies immediate group identity API at :607–909. MinimalAxioms.lean:39 and :66 prove equivalent minimal-axiom constructors. Inspected selected proof bodies and found no sorry/admit/axiom declarations in these three files. File selection is the defining group layer and immediate identity/constructor API; no downstream group theory, transport, opposite/product structures, homomorphism theory or parent monoid hierarchy is charged here. Bounded file selection and excluded candidates are recorded in data/formalization-pilot-review.txt; availability does not certify an exhaustive API inventory.

Inspected upstream Mathlib commit 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. CommGroup at Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean:116 extends Group and CommMonoid, exactly a group with commutative multiplication; AddCommGroup at :111 is its additive form. CommGroup.toCancelCommMonoid (:124) and toDivisionCommMonoid (:129) provide the immediate commutative hierarchy. Basic.lean has explicit commutative inverse/division/power identities under DivisionCommMonoid at :516–605 and CommGroup at :912–1016, including mul_inv (:523), mul_zpow (:593), div_div_cancel (:943), and div_eq_div_iff_mul_eq_mul (:996). Proof bodies inspected; no sorry/admit/axiom declarations in these two files. Only defining and immediate law API files are selected, not every general-group file whose facts apply by inheritance. Bounded file selection and excluded candidates are recorded in data/formalization-pilot-review.txt; availability does not certify an exhaustive API inventory.

Inspected Tau Ceti commit 3780371ca1bebf9f1c2bb3d753e4bb56c9526023. Its lake-manifest.json pins Mathlib 2ddf59c8f14245864e6c0ed227a2dab76b9efea2; inspected that dependency commit directly and confirmed Group/AddGroup at Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean:33/:44 and both inverse laws. Tau Ceti supplies no new generic Group definition, but its own TauCeti/Algebra/Group/Pow.lean:58–60 proves eq_mul_zpow_sub_iff_mul_zpow_eq for an arbitrary Group, an immediate integer-power equation law. The proof is an explicit derivation from zpow_sub, associativity and inverse cancellation, without placeholders or an assumed endpoint. On the agreed pilot interpretation, formalized means the definition is available (including dependencies) and this project owns qualifying direct API; only Tau Ceti-owned API files contribute its LOC.
